# Review of beowulf-fitt-18 (lines 1192-1250)

Two passes. Pass 1 on the drafted units.json (every note label, then OE to l word by word, l to i, remembered English, consistency with the published parts). Pass 2 on the revised file, plus gloss.json (which existed when pass 1 finished; every parse checked against its line and against the units' notes). `t` was never touched (verified: every `t` is still a contiguous cut of the packet's lines, in order). Severity: high = a false statement or wrong sense; medium = wrong or unsupported rendering or note claim; low = polish, consistency, softening.

## Findings considered and refused

- 1210 i "with his breast-armor and the ring together": the syntax is looser than the OE (three subjects), but "with ... together" is ordinary English for the sense. Left.
- 1233 "swā hit āgangen wearð" as pluperfect "had come to pass": wearð is preterite, but Klaeber's connection to the coming night makes the pluperfect an acceptable reading; the note says the poet looks ahead. Left.
- 1192 l "favors" against n "graces": both gloss ēst; left.
- 1246 l "both each of them": literal for gē gehwæþer; apparatus noted in n. Left.
- 1204 "since"/"after"/"when" for syþðan across units: sense decides each (1198 "since" with a past event; 1204, 1205 "after"); kept.
- 1220 i "I will not forget to reward you": a paraphrase of gemunan, but built from the grammar; not a recognised phrase. Left.
- 1240 "beer-men" vs "beer-drinkers": l literal, i interpretive; consistent with the convention.
- 1218a/1226 "suna" singular against "cnyhtum" plural: the note says so; no change to the text.
- The two cruxes (flēah at 1200; windgeard weallas at 1224) are not entered in QUESTIONS.md; the conventions ask for that for a famous crux. Not done by the reviewer (outside the files named); flag for the drafter.
